================================================================================
TY TYPE CHECKER CONFIGURATION FOR VSCODE
================================================================================

SETUP COMPLETED: ✅

The fleet-rlm repository has been configured to use ty, a strict Python type 
checker, within VSCode.

================================================================================
FILES CREATED/MODIFIED
================================================================================

1. .vscode/settings.json (MODIFIED)
   - Added python.linting.enabled: true
   - Added python.testing.pytestEnabled: true
   - Added files.exclude for .ty_cache directories

2. .vscode/tasks.json (NEW)
   - "ty: Check types" — single check execution
   - "ty: Watch types" — continuous file watching
   - "ty: Explain rules" — rule documentation viewer

3. .vscode/keybindings.json (NEW)
   - Ctrl+Shift+T keyboard shortcut for quick type checking

4. .vscode/launch.json (NEW)
   - Standard Python debugging configurations
   - FastAPI-specific launch configuration

5. .vscode/README_TY_CONFIG.md (NEW)
   - Complete documentation on ty integration
   - Usage instructions and troubleshooting

================================================================================
QUICK START
================================================================================

1. Open the project in VSCode
2. Press Ctrl+Shift+T to run a type check
3. Or run "ty: Watch types" task from Command Palette for continuous checking
4. Check .vscode/README_TY_CONFIG.md for detailed documentation

================================================================================
INTEGRATION LEVEL
================================================================================

Current Integration: TASK + PROBLEM MATCHER BASED

✅ Supported:
   - Task-based single checks
   - Watch mode for continuous checks
   - Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+T)
   - Problem matcher for inline error display
   - Cache exclusion for clean UI
   - Debug launch configurations

❌ Not Supported (VSCode Python extension limitation):
   - Real-time LSP-based diagnostics
   - Direct integration with Python extension's type checker dropdown

Note: VSCode's Python extension (>= 2024.x) does not yet support ty as a 
native type checker option. This configuration uses tasks and problem matchers 
as a workaround. When VSCode adds native ty support, this configuration can be 
simplified.

================================================================================
COMMANDS
================================================================================

Local development:
  make typecheck              # Run: uv run ty check src
  ty check --watch           # Continuous checking
  ty explain                 # View rule documentation

VSCode Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P):
  - Tasks: Run Task → "ty: Check types"
  - Tasks: Run Task → "ty: Watch types"

================================================================================
TY CONFIGURATION
================================================================================

Configuration file: pyproject.toml

[tool.ty.src]
exclude = [
    "tests/",
    "scripts/",
    "notebooks/",
    "test_modal_guard.py",
    "setup.py",
]

Version: ty 0.0.34

================================================================================
NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

Optional enhancements:

1. Add ty to pre-commit hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml
2. Configure team's VSCode extensions recommendations in extensions.json
3. Monitor VSCode Python extension for native ty support
4. Consider ty LSP client extensions if real-time diagnostics become critical
